title: Consequence-based review gate
summary: Use the plausible consequences of an AI-assisted change to decide whether it can follow routine review or needs deeper scrutiny. The decision path records the reasoning, evidence, reviewer, and required next action.
prerequisites: A description of the proposed change and its intended outcome
Evidence from testing or evaluation of the proposed change
An accountable person who can approve, reject, or defer the change

sections.title: Choose the review path
paragraphs: When should an AI-assisted change receive deeper review? Send it to deeper review when a plausible failure could cause consequential harm, affect a broad group, or be difficult to reverse. Otherwise, use the routine review path while retaining the evidence that supports that decision. This is an intermediate-level decision path, so it assumes that testing evidence and an accountable decision owner already exist.

Step 1: Describe the proposed change, its intended outcome, the people or systems it could affect, and the plausible consequences of failure. If the affected parties or consequences cannot be identified, pause the decision and ask the accountable owner to supply the missing context before review continues.

Step 2: Consider the severity, scope, and reversibility of each plausible consequence. If the available evidence cannot support that assessment, classify the uncertainty as unresolved and use the deeper review path until additional testing or evaluation resolves it.

Step 3: Select the review path. Use deeper review when any plausible consequence is consequential, broad in scope, difficult to reverse, or materially uncertain. Use routine review only when the recorded evidence supports the lower-consequence decision. If reviewers disagree, do not average their judgments; defer the change to the accountable owner or a reviewer with authority to resolve the disagreement.

Step 4: Record the decision, supporting evidence, reviewer, unresolved uncertainty, and required follow-up. If no accountable reviewer is available or the record is incomplete, do not proceed with the change; return it to the owner for assignment or completion.
sections.callout: The gate does not prove that a change is safe. It determines the level of scrutiny justified by the consequences and uncertainty documented for that change.

sections.title: Source correction
paragraphs: The cited source changed. The previous citation, content/resources/research-verification/consequence-based-review-gate.json, was an internal path from an unregistered publisher and had never been verified. It has been replaced with the official publication listed in the sources field.

This correction affects the attribution and verification basis for the guide. The replacement source supports considering context, impacts, risk, documentation, and accountability when managing AI risk. The decision thresholds in this resource remain a local review procedure rather than thresholds prescribed by the source.

No tool name, version requirement, or configuration key is needed for this provider-neutral gate. If local policy defines stricter review criteria, apply that policy and record which criterion controlled the decision. If the applicable local policy cannot be identified, pause the change and ask the accountable owner to identify it.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence is a decision record containing the proposed change, intended outcome, affected people or systems, plausible failure consequences, assessment of severity, scope and reversibility, unresolved uncertainty, selected review path, supporting evidence, reviewer, and required follow-up.

Verify the result by asking a reviewer who did not prepare the record to follow the decision path using only the recorded information. The verification succeeds when that reviewer can identify the same review path and locate evidence for each required consideration. If the reviewer reaches a different path or cannot find the evidence, treat verification as failed and return the record for clarification, additional evaluation, or deeper review.

Before the change proceeds, confirm that unresolved high-consequence or difficult-to-reverse outcomes were not assigned to routine review. If that confirmation cannot be made, stop the change and escalate it to the accountable owner.
